comparison_summary: SRP only vs SRP + systemic doxycycline vs no treatment (control)
intervention_description: Full mouth scaling and root planing under local anesthesia, plus oral hygiene instructions.

comparison_summary: SRP only vs SRP + systemic doxycycline vs no treatment (control)
intervention_description: Full mouth scaling and root planing under local anesthesia plus oral hygiene instructions, and systemic doxycycline 100 mg (DOXY-1, USV Pharmaceuticals), two tablets on the first day, followed by one tablet daily for 14 days.

comparison_summary: SRP only vs SRP + systemic doxycycline vs no treatment (control)
intervention_description: No oral hygiene instructions and full mouth scaling and root planing was not performed in these patients.

comparison_summary: periodontal therapy vs no intervention (control) in patients with T2DM and chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: All subjects in the intervention group underwent a periodontal intervention that included oral hygiene (utilizing correct methods and soft-bristled toothbrushes, interdental brushes and dental floss), full-mouth scaling (supragingival and subgingival scaling), the extraction of hopeless teeth, and the restoration of balanced occlusion. All periodontal interventions were completed by a single periodontist (Jingsong Liu) within two weeks.

comparison_summary: periodontal therapy vs no periodontal intervention
intervention_description: No periodontal intervention. No changes in medications or diet were made for any subject during the study period.

comparison_summary: Supragingival therapy (ST) vs intensive periodontal therapy (IT; supra- and subgingival scaling and root planing)
intervention_description: Supragingival scaling using an ultrasonic device and periodontal curettes (Hu-Friedy®, Chicago, USA). A single appointment lasted ~60 minutes. Supportive therapy for biofilm control consisted of professional instructions on oral hygiene given to each patient every month.

comparison_summary: supragingival scaling (ST) vs supra- and subgingival scaling and root planing (IT)
intervention_description: Supra- and subgingival scaling and root planing (in sites with PPD ≥ 4 mm) using an ultrasonic device and periodontal curettes (Hu-Friedy®, Chicago, USA). Performed under local anesthesia (3% prilocaine with felypressin), in two appointments lasting ~120 minutes each. Supportive therapy for biofilm control consisted of professional instructions on oral hygiene given to each patient every month.

comparison_summary: SRP (OHI + scaling and root planing) vs supragingival scaling (OHI + supragingival removal of plaque and calculus)
intervention_description: oral hygiene instructions + scaling and root planing using ultrasound and Gracey curettes (full-mouth debridement)

comparison_summary: SRP (oral hygiene instructions + scaling and root planing) vs supragingival scaling (oral hygiene instructions + supragingival removal of plaque and calculus)
intervention_description: oral hygiene instructions + supragingival removal of plaque and calculus using ultrasound (Satelec P5 Newtron XS)

comparison_summary: scaling+mouthwash+brushing (Group A) vs mouthwash+brushing (Group B) vs brushing only (Group C)
intervention_description: Scaling, plus 0.12% chlorhexidine mouthwash (once daily), and brushing (twice daily)

comparison_summary: scaling + mouthwash + brushing (Group A) vs mouthwash + brushing (Group B) vs brushing only (Group C)
intervention_description: 0.12% chlorhexidine mouthwash (once daily) and brushing (twice daily), no scaling

comparison_summary: scaling + mouthwash + brushing (Group A) vs mouthwash + brushing (Group B) vs brushing only (Group C)
intervention_description: Brushing only (twice daily)

comparison_summary: SRP vs untreated control
intervention_description: Oral health instructions, supra-/subgingival scaling (Cavitron Bobcat Pro, Dentsply, York, PA, USA), and manual curettage (Hu-Friedy, Chicago, IL, USA), completed within 2 weeks after the baseline evaluation.

comparison_summary: SRP vs no periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: No periodontal treatment; evaluations at baseline and at 3 and 6 months only.

comparison_summary: SRP vs no treatment (control); sub-ERP vs prophylaxis (within treatment group)
intervention_description: Full-mouth ultrasonic scaling and manual root planing of the teeth with PPD ≥ 4 mm (enhanced root planing, ERP).

comparison_summary: SRP vs no treatment (control); sub-ERP vs subprophylaxis
intervention_description: Full-mouth ultrasonic scaling only to remove calculus and plaque (prophylaxis).

comparison_summary: immediate periodontal therapy (SRP + antibiotics + OHI) vs delayed periodontal therapy (no active treatment during follow-up)
intervention_description: Immediate periodontal therapy: full-mouth SRP performed in a single two-hour session using ultrasonic apparatus (Cavitron Select SPC, Dentsply professional) and Gracey curettes (Hu-Friedy), with local anesthesia when needed. SRP was associated with subgingival irrigation by chlorhexidine 0.12% mouthwash (Peridex oral rinse, 3M ESPE Dental Products). Immediately after SRP, administration of systemic antibiotics: metronidazole 400 mg three times daily for 2 weeks and amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily for 2 weeks. Plus oral hygiene instructions.

comparison_summary: immediate non-surgical periodontal therapy (SRP + antibiotics + OHI) vs delayed periodontal therapy (no active treatment during follow-up)
intervention_description: Delayed periodontal therapy — no active periodontal therapies were done during the 3-month follow-up period. The same procedures applied to the test group were performed after the end of the follow-up period (3 months) for ethical reasons.

comparison_summary: SRP vs no treatment in type 2 diabetes patients stratified by baseline HbA1c (good vs poor glycemic control), with nondiabetic comparator group
intervention_description: Nonsurgical periodontal treatment comprising four SRP sessions over a maximum of 2 weeks, using standard rigid Gracey curettes (Hu-Friedy Manufacturing Co.) and an ultrasonic scaler (Suprasson P5 Booster, Satelec-Acteon group.). Oral hygiene instructions were given at baseline and reviewed at each visit.

comparison_summary: Nonsurgical periodontal therapy (SRP) vs no treatment in patients with type 2 diabetes stratified by glycemic control (good vs poor), with nondiabetic SRP controls
intervention_description: Nonsurgical periodontal treatment comprising four SRP sessions over a maximum of 2 weeks, using standard rigid Gracey curettes (Hu-Friedy Manufacturing Co.) and an ultrasonic scaler (Suprasson P5 Booster, Satelec-Acteon group.). Oral hygiene instructions were given at baseline and reviewed at each visit.

comparison_summary: SRP (nonsurgical periodontal therapy) vs no treatment in T2DM patients with good or poor glycemic control vs nondiabetic individuals
intervention_description: No periodontal treatment during the study period. Periodontal treatment was performed after completion of the study (after 6 months).

comparison_summary: SRP vs no treatment in patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic periodontitis, stratified by glycemic control (good vs poor), plus nondiabetic comparator
intervention_description: No periodontal treatment during the study period. Periodontal treatment was performed after completion of the study (after 6 months).

comparison_summary: SRP (treatment group) vs no treatment (no-treatment group) in T2DM patients with good vs poor glycemic control, plus nondiabetic comparator group receiving SRP
intervention_description: Nonsurgical periodontal treatment comprising four SRP sessions over a maximum of 2 weeks, using standard rigid Gracey curettes (Hu-Friedy Manufacturing Co.) and an ultrasonic scaler (Suprasson P5 Booster, Satelec-Acteon group.). Oral hygiene instructions were given at baseline and reviewed at each visit.

comparison_summary: SRP plus oral hygiene instructions vs oral hygiene instructions alone
intervention_description: Scaling and root planing (SRP) performed with an ultrasonic scaler (Dentsply, York, PA, USA) and Gracey curettes (Hu-Friedy, Chicago, IL, USA). Two quadrants were instrumented at each appointment under local anaesthesia, using 2% lidocaine with 1:100,000 epinephrine (Dentsply), with an endpoint of achieving smooth root surfaces. The procedure was performed by two calibrated periodontists. Oral hygiene instructions including the modified Bass technique, use of inter-proximal toothbrushes and dental floss were also provided.

comparison_summary: SRP vs oral hygiene instructions only
intervention_description: Oral hygiene instructions only, including the modified Bass technique, use of inter-proximal toothbrushes and dental floss. No professional mechanical/subgingival instrumentation was performed during the study period.

comparison_summary: SRP + subgingival debridement vs SRP + supragingival prophylaxis vs no treatment (control)
intervention_description: Non-surgical periodontal treatment consisting of scaling and root planing under local anesthesia at baseline, completed within 24 hours by an experienced periodontist using standard rigid periodontal curets and ultrasonic instrumentation, without antibiotics or local antimicrobials; plus additional subgingival debridement at the 3-month follow-up.

comparison_summary: SRP + subgingival debridement vs SRP + supragingival prophylaxis vs no treatment (control)
intervention_description: Non-surgical periodontal treatment consisting of scaling and root planing under local anesthesia at baseline, completed within 24 hours by an experienced periodontist using standard rigid periodontal curets and ultrasonic instrumentation, without antibiotics or local antimicrobials; plus supragingival prophylaxis with no intervention in deep periodontal pockets at the 3-month follow-up.

comparison_summary: SRP + subgingival debridement vs SRP + supragingival prophylaxis vs no treatment (control)
intervention_description: No treatment measure or formal oral hygiene instructions throughout the study period.

comparison_summary: immediate NSPT vs delayed periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: Immediate nonsurgical periodontal treatment: full mouth debridement in a single visit consisting of scaling, root scaling and planning using a magneto-restrictive ultrasonic device and Gracey's cures, followed by sub-gingival irrigation with a 10% povidone iodine solution. Additionally, subjects received dental floss and chlorhexidine gluconate 0.2% as mouth wash (10 ml twice daily for 5 days). All subjects were instructed in oral hygiene methods using the modified Bass technique.

comparison_summary: immediate NSPT (scaling, root planning + povidone iodine irrigation) vs delayed periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: Delayed periodontal treatment: no interventional treatment was given during the follow-up, apart from oral hygiene instructions. At the end of the study, all participants in the control group received the treatment as the treatment group.

comparison_summary: non-surgical periodontal treatment (immediate) vs delayed non-surgical periodontal treatment
intervention_description: Non-surgical periodontal treatment: motivational intervention with oral hygiene instructions, then scaling and root planing under local anesthesia in four sessions within 24 h (45 min per quadrant) using an ultrasonic scaler (PIEZO-soft ultrasonic scaler; KaVo Dental, Germany) equipped with PIEZO Scaler Tip 201, and manual instruments (Gracey Curettes). Ultrasonic instrumentation performed in apical to cervical direction using linear oscillations at 30 KHz with medium power setting. Subgingival irrigation with chlorhexidine 0.12% associated.

comparison_summary: non-surgical periodontal treatment (immediate) vs delayed non-surgical periodontal treatment
intervention_description: Delayed non-surgical periodontal treatment (no active periodontal treatment during the 6-month follow-up period). At the end of the 6-month follow-up period the non-surgical periodontal treatment was carried out for the control group, performing the same procedures as the intervention group, for an ethical reason.

comparison_summary: NSPT vs OHI
intervention_description: Full mouth debridement consisting of scaling and root planing done in a single visit using an ultrasonic scaler (SATELEC P5 Newtron XS) and Gracey curettes, plus oral hygiene instructions, plus 0.12% Chlorhexidine mouthrinse (Hexipro) three times a day using 15 ml each time for 14 days. Monthly recall visits with professional prophylaxis (scaling and polishing).

comparison_summary: NSPT vs OHI
intervention_description: No interventional treatment given apart from oral hygiene instructions and motivation. All subjects were instructed in oral hygiene methods using a soft bristled toothbrush, a compact-tuft toothbrush, interdental brushes and dental floss (TePe® oral hygiene education set) utilising the modified Bass technique. Monthly recall visits with OHI only.

comparison_summary: Early Treatment (SRP + doxycycline + chlorhexidine) vs Usual Care
intervention_description: Early Treatment for 4 months (periodontal scaling and root planing until smooth root surfaces were achieved plus doxycycline [100 mg by mouth daily for 14 days] and chlorhexidine gluconate [CHX] rinses [30 cc, 0.12%, twice daily for 4 months]), then Usual Care.

comparison_summary: Early Treatment (periodontal care) vs Usual Care
intervention_description: By Usual Care we mean that the participants used did not alter their medical and dental care routine; rather, they proceeded with their health care as usual. For some this meant that they used dental and medical services, for others it did not.

comparison_summary: SRP vs SRP + doxycycline vs no treatment (control)
intervention_description: Oral hygiene instructions and full mouth scaling and root planing (SRP)

comparison_summary: SRP vs SRP + doxycycline vs no periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: Oral hygiene instructions and full mouth SRP plus systemic doxycycline (total dose 1,600 mg in equally divided 16 doses, start as 100 mg BD followed by OD for 14 days)

comparison_summary: SRP vs SRP + doxycycline vs no periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: No periodontal treatment administered during the 3-month study period

comparison_summary: anti-infectious periodontal treatment (mechanical debridement + topical minocycline) vs. no periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: Mechanical debridement of the sub-gingival plaque and calculus was performed using piezo-electric ultra sonic scalers, and 10 mg of minocycline ointment (Periofil®, Showa Yakuhin Co., Tokyo, Japan) was administered topically in every periodontal pocket at the end of each visit. The intensive periodontal treatment was completed over the course of four visits within 2 months. After completion, additional periodontal treatment including instructions for brushing, supra- and sub-gingival debridement without topical administration of antibiotics were performed, if necessary, at 1, 3 and 6 month follow-up visits.

comparison_summary: anti-infectious periodontal treatment (mechanical debridement + topical minocycline) vs non-periodontal treatment (oral hygiene instructions only)
intervention_description: Control group participants received instructions for brushing their teeth, including the use of inter-proximal cleaning aids, such as floss and inter-dental brushes, depending on their individual needs.

comparison_summary: non-surgical periodontal scaling vs untreated control
intervention_description: An untimed single episode of non-surgical periodontal therapy comprising supra- and subgingival scaling using Gracey curettes (Hu-Friedy, Chicago, USA), and piezoelectric ultrasonic device (Kyungwon Ferrite, Gyeonggi-Do, South Korea) with universal tips. To complete the intervention, a full-mouth dental prophylaxis using a rubber cup and Ainsworth prophylaxis paste (Ainsworth Dental Company, Sydney, Australia) was provided to remove plaque and tooth stains. Local anaesthesia was administered as required. All participants received oral hygiene advice consisting of toothbrush and flossing instructions and were provided with a toothbrush and toothpaste at baseline.

comparison_summary: non-surgical periodontal therapy (full-mouth scaling) vs untreated control
intervention_description: Untreated at baseline; periodontal intervention was delayed for 12 months. All participants received oral hygiene advice consisting of toothbrush and flossing instructions and were provided with a toothbrush and toothpaste at baseline.

comparison_summary: tooth extraction alone vs. tooth extraction combined with FM-SRP (non-surgical periodontal treatment) in T2DM and non-diabetic patients with periodontal disease
intervention_description: At least one tooth was extracted from each patient. The control group did not receive any other treatment until the 3-month follow-up.

arm_label: T2DM - Tooth Extraction and FM-SRP (treatment group)
comparison_summary: tooth extraction alone vs. tooth extraction + FM-SRP (with Listerine mouthrinse)
intervention_description: At least one tooth was extracted. Prior to the surgical procedures, an adjunctive, non-surgical periodontal treatment to achieve a full-mouth tooth cleaning was performed: Full-Mouth Scaling and Root Planning (FM-SRP) using an ultrasonic device (UDS-J Ultrasonic Scaler, Guilin Woodpecker Medical Instrument) and periodontal currettes for the mechanical debridement of supra- and subgingival plaque and calculus. Post-operative rinsing with Listerine® (ethanol 21.6%, methyl salicylate 0.06%, menthol 0.042%, thymol 0.064% and eucalyptol 0.092%) as a mouthwash thrice a day for 3 w.

comparison_summary: tooth extraction only vs tooth extraction + FM-SRP (non-surgical periodontal treatment) in T2DM and non-diabetic patients with periodontitis
intervention_description: At least one tooth was extracted. No additional periodontal treatment was received until the 3-month follow-up.

comparison_summary: tooth extraction alone vs. tooth extraction combined with FM-SRP (in T2DM and non-diabetic patients with periodontitis)
intervention_description: At least one tooth was extracted. Prior to the surgical procedures, an adjunctive, non-surgical periodontal treatment to achieve a full-mouth tooth cleaning was performed: Full-Mouth Scaling and Root Planning (FM-SRP) using an ultrasonic device (UDS-J Ultrasonic Scaler, Guilin Woodpecker Medical Instrument) and periodontal currettes for the mechanical debridement of supra- and subgingival plaque and calculus. Post-operative rinsing with Listerine® as a mouthwash thrice a day for 3 w.

comparison_summary: SRP + MET + OHI vs SRP + OHI vs OHI only (control)
intervention_description: SRP through ultrasonic scaling (average 60 min on medium intensity full mouth in single sitting) and hand instrumentation (sharpened and sterilized curettes) to smoothen root surface, followed by metronidazole (MET) 400 mg × 3 for 10 days, warm salt water rinses for 3–5 days, and oral hygiene instructions (OHI).

comparison_summary: SRP+MET+OHI vs SRP+OHI vs OHI only (control)
intervention_description: SRP through ultrasonic scaling and hand instrumentation plus oral hygiene instructions (OHI), without metronidazole.

comparison_summary: SRP+MET+OHI vs SRP+OHI vs OHI only (control)
intervention_description: Oral hygiene instructions (OHI) only, with periodontal therapy provided at end of trial (delayed treatment, DT).

comparison_summary: scaling and root planning plus doxycycline (group A) vs doxycycline alone/no periodontal treatment (group B)
intervention_description: Scaling and root planning plus systemic doxycycline 100 mg/day for 14 days. Five 60-minute appointments on a weekly basis: first appointment included intensive oral health instruction, supragingival scaling and polishing; subsequent appointments included oral hygiene monitoring and subgingival scaling and root planning under topical anaesthesia on a quadrant-by-quadrant basis.

comparison_summary: SRP plus doxycycline (group A) vs no periodontal treatment plus doxycycline (group B)
intervention_description: Temporarily without periodontal treatment (control group), plus systemic doxycycline 100 mg/day for 14 days. Subjects acted as a non-treatment control group for the duration of the study, then treated in the same manner as group A after 16 weeks.

comparison_summary: periodontal surgery (modified Widman flap) vs supportive periodontal therapy
intervention_description: Modified Widman flap procedures performed in areas with deep pockets. Reverse incisions, full thickness mucoperiosteal flaps raised, granulation tissue removed, root instrumentation performed, alveolar bone shape corrected. Flaps replaced to original position and secured with sutures removed 1 week after surgery.

comparison_summary: periodontal surgery vs supportive periodontal treatment
intervention_description: Scaling and root planning on diseased root surfaces. Subjects advised to rinse with 0.2% chlorhexidine solution twice daily for 2 weeks.

comparison_summary: scaling and root planing plus chlorhexidine oral rinse and supportive periodontal therapy vs no periodontal treatment (oral hygiene instructions only)
intervention_description: Scaling and root planing plus chlorhexidine oral rinse at baseline and supportive periodontal therapy at 3 and 6 months. Initial treatment consisted of at least 160 minutes of scaling and root planing using currettes and ultrasonic instruments with local anesthesia during 2 or more sessions completed within 42 days of the baseline visit. After treatment, the therapist provided oral hygiene instructions and dispensed chlorhexidine gluconate (0.12% oral rinse, twice daily for 2 weeks), toothbrush, toothpaste, and dental floss. Three and 6 months after the baseline visit, participants received oral hygiene instructions and scaling and root planing for approximately 1 hour during a single session.

comparison_summary: scaling and root planing plus supportive periodontal therapy vs no periodontal treatment (oral hygiene instructions only)
intervention_description: No periodontal treatment for 6 months. Participants received only oral hygiene instructions at the baseline and 3- and 6-month visits. Following their 6-month visit, control group participants were offered scaling and root planing.

comparison_summary: IPT (intensive periodontal treatment) vs CPT (control periodontal treatment)
intervention_description: Whole mouth subgingival scaling of the root surfaces under local analgesia (single session, no time limit); at 2 months, patients with good oral hygiene (plaque scores ≤20%) and at least one 6 mm or deeper residual periodontal pocket received periodontal surgical therapy; those with suboptimum oral hygiene or no residual 6 mm pockets received additional scaling under local analgesia; all IPT patients subsequently received further sessions of scaling of the root surfaces under local analgesia every 3 months until completion of the study.

comparison_summary: IPT (intensive periodontal treatment) vs CPT (control periodontal treatment)
intervention_description: Supra-gingival scaling and polishing of all dentition at the same timepoints as the IPT group (after baseline and at 2, 6, 9, and 12 months after the completion of the first session of periodontal therapy). At the end of the study, patients in the CPT group received any additional periodontal therapy that was required.

comparison_summary: full-mouth scaling and root planing vs no periodontal treatment
intervention_description: Full-mouth scaling and root planing performed under local anaesthesia, plus oral hygiene instructions.

comparison_summary: full-mouth scaling and root planing vs no periodontal treatment
intervention_description: No periodontal treatment during the study period.

comparison_summary: OHI plus scaling and root debridement vs OHI alone
intervention_description: Oral hygiene instruction (OHI) plus non-surgical periodontal therapy including extraction of hopeless teeth, scaling and root debridement with both hand instruments and ultrasonic scaler. Review appointments were given every 4–6 weeks to reinforce patients' plaque control.

comparison_summary: OHI + scaling and root debridement vs OHI alone
intervention_description: Oral hygiene instruction (OHI) alone, with no active periodontal treatment during the 6-month study period.

comparison_summary: immediate periodontal treatment vs delayed periodontal treatment (no treatment control)
intervention_description: Periodontal treatment included non-surgical scaling and root planing (SRP), systemic antibiotics (amoxicillin 2 g/day for 7 days after periodontal treatment) and providing a supply of oral hygiene products and oral health instructions. SRP was performed over the 10-day period following the inclusion visit. SRP was performed in a single 2-hr session. Dental surgeons performed full-mouth ultrasonic and hand instrument debridement. Local anaesthesia was administered if necessary. SRP was accompanied by subgingival irrigation with an antiseptic mouthwash (chlorhexidine 0.12%). After SRP, subjects received personalized oral health instructions (OHI) and a free pack containing all the dental care products needed for 3 months of periodontal maintenance.

comparison_summary: immediate periodontal treatment vs delayed (no) periodontal treatment
intervention_description: Delayed periodontal treatment for the control group was performed with exactly the same procedures at the end of the 3-month follow-up period for ethical reasons. Therefore, the control group was a true 'no treatment' control arm for which no periodontal procedure was performed during the follow-up.

comparison_summary: non-surgical periodontal treatment (SRP + oral hygiene instructions) vs oral hygiene instructions only (control)
intervention_description: Non-surgical periodontal therapy consisting of at least 60 minutes of scaling and root planing using curettes and an ultrasonic instrument during 2 or more sessions completed within 42 days after the baseline visit, plus oral hygiene instructions, professional toothbrushing and mechanical tooth cleaning. At 3 and 6 months, participants received periodontal maintenance therapy including oral hygiene instructions and oral prophylaxis for approximately 1 hour during a single session.

comparison_summary: non-surgical periodontal treatment vs oral hygiene instructions only (no periodontal treatment)
intervention_description: Oral hygiene instructions only at the baseline and 3 and 6 month visits, without any periodontal treatment during the experimental period.

comparison_summary: SRP (intervention group) vs supragingival prophylaxis/minimal treatment (control group)
intervention_description: Full-mouth scaling and root planing (SRP), in two sessions, 1 week apart, with the use of an ultrasonic scaler (Minipiezon Electromedical Systems EMS, Nyon, Switzerland) and hand instruments, under local anaesthesia. All subjects received oral hygiene instructions after each visit, while the IG received additional supportive SRP at each visit, if judged necessary (presence of sites with BOP and/or increased PPD).

comparison_summary: SRP (intervention group) vs supragingival prophylaxis/delayed treatment (control group)
intervention_description: Periodontal prophylaxis at baseline, in the form of supragingival removal of all deposits (plaque and calculus) with an ultrasonic scaler. SRP was performed in the CG after the completion of the study (after the 6-month visit). All subjects received oral hygiene instructions after each visit.

comparison_summary: T2DM-T (periodontal intervention) vs T2DM-NT (no periodontal intervention)
intervention_description: No periodontal intervention (control group; diabetes management continued without changes to medication during the 3-month study period)

comparison_summary: T2DM-T (periodontal intervention) vs T2DM-NT (no periodontal intervention)
intervention_description: Periodontal intervention included oral hygiene, full-mouth scaling (supragingival and subgingival scaling), root planning, periodontal flap surgery when indicated, and extraction of hopeless teeth, restore of balanced occlusion. Antibiotics (Tinidazole 1.0 g, bid, po. and ampicillin 0.25 g, qid, po.) were prescribed for 3 days before and after periodontal intervention.

comparison_summary: SRP vs SRPAT (SRP with additional toothbrushing) vs control
intervention_description: After a baseline oral examination, oral health education including toothbrush instruction was conducted. In the SRP group, supragingival scaling was performed only on the first visit by 2 trained dentists working together simultaneously. After 2 weeks, root planing was performed to remove the subgingival calculus. At 12 weeks, patients were recalled to re-check their oral health status.

comparison_summary: SRP vs SRPAT (SRP with additional toothbrushing) vs control
intervention_description: After a baseline oral examination, oral health education including toothbrush instruction was conducted. In the SRPAT group, additional toothbrushing (Watanabe method) with a 2-row toothbrush was applied on the first visit by a trained dentist. On the second visit, subgingival calculus was removed as appropriate according to the patient's oral health condition. Additional toothbrushing (Watanabe method) was performed once a week from the first visit through the fifth visit.

comparison_summary: SRP vs SRPAT (SRP with additional toothbrushing) vs control
intervention_description: The CTR group received no other treatments beyond medical screening for diabetes. However, all groups received oral health education including toothbrush instruction at the baseline visit to eliminate intergroup bias associated with routine oral health behaviours. After the study was completed, the necessary dental treatment was provided to the patients who wished to receive it.
